title: Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — Premium Revision Paper #9

pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #9
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why do we keep a class portfolio of songs? (1 mark)
   A. So the songs are kept safe and are not forgotten
   B. To throw them away
   C. To hide them
   D. To sell them

2. Which is the key question of this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. What is the price of food?
   B. How far is the market?
   C. Who is the tallest pupil?
   D. How should we respond to instructions?

3. What is a good way to give feedback to a reader? (1 mark)
   A. Laugh at mistakes
   B. Say they are bad
   C. Say one good thing and one thing to improve
   D. Say nothing

4. How can flashcards help with vocabulary? (1 mark)
   A. They let you practise a word and its meaning again and again
   B. They replace reading
   C. They cost a lot
   D. They make words disappear

5. Which letter hangs below the base line in English handwriting? (1 mark)
   A. o
   B. c
   C. a
   D. g

6. In English, what usually happens to the voice at the end of a question? (1 mark)
   A. It stays exactly the same always
   B. It falls to silence
   C. It becomes a whisper
   D. It rises

7. A newsreader on the radio should speak (1 mark)
   A. clearly and at a steady pace
   B. in a whisper
   C. with no pauses
   D. very fast

8. Which is a common mistake? (1 mark)
   A. Using a comma in a list
   B. Starting a sentence with a capital
   C. Ending with a full stop
   D. Using a comma where a full stop is needed

9. Which habit helps you listen well? (1 mark)
   A. Sitting where you can see and hear the speaker
   B. Playing with a pencil
   C. Looking at the floor
   D. Talking to a neighbour

10. Which question word asks about a person? (1 mark)
   A. When
   B. Where
   C. How many
   D. Who

11. Which of these is a safety rule from the road safety dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. Play on the road
   B. Run across without looking
   C. Look right, then left, then right again
   D. Cross anywhere

12. In The road was congested and the matatu could not move, what does congested mean? (1 mark)
   A. Very clean
   B. Very wide
   C. Very short
   D. Very crowded

13. Which sentence should come first when making tea? (1 mark)
   A. First, boil the water.
   B. Finally, serve the tea.
   C. Then pour the milk.
   D. Next, drink it.

14. What is the best way to check the order of your paragraph? (1 mark)
   A. Copy it
   B. Fold the page
   C. Read it aloud
   D. Cover it

15. Which words signal a simile? (1 mark)
   A. but and or
   B. is and are
   C. to and from
   D. like and as

16. Which sentence is a metaphor? (1 mark)
   A. The classroom was busy.
   B. The classroom was like a beehive.
   C. The classroom was a beehive.
   D. The classroom was as busy as a beehive.

17. Which sentence is a simile? (1 mark)
   A. She is a sun.
   B. She is bright.
   C. She is as bright as the sun.
   D. She is a shining star.

18. What is a skit? (1 mark)
   A. A picture
   B. A long poem
   C. A list
   D. A short play

19. What should you do if a classmate's story is not as good as yours? (1 mark)
   A. Interrupt
   B. Laugh at them
   C. Listen politely and give kind feedback
   D. Leave

20. What is a customer? (1 mark)
   A. A type of money
   B. A person who sells only
   C. A kind of shop
   D. A person who buys

21. What is skimming? (1 mark)
   A. Reading quickly to get the main idea
   B. Reading backwards
   C. Copying the text
   D. Reading slowly for every word

22. What does a simple sentence have? (1 mark)
   A. No capital
   B. Two subjects always
   C. No verb
   D. One subject and one predicate

23. What is a bargain? (1 mark)
   A. To steal
   B. To run
   C. To discuss the price
   D. To sleep

24. In front of means (1 mark)
   A. before something and facing it
   B. inside it
   C. behind it
   D. under it

25. Which is a domestic animal? (1 mark)
   A. Elephant
   B. Zebra
   C. Lion
   D. Goat

26. In choral recitation, the group (1 mark)
   A. sings only
   B. says the poem together at the same pace
   C. reads silently
   D. writes the poem

27. Which is a good tip for reciting? (1 mark)
   A. Look at the audience and speak clearly
   B. Speak very fast
   C. Cover your face
   D. Look at the floor and mumble

28. What is a hobby? (1 mark)
   A. A test
   B. A school rule
   C. A punishment
   D. Something you enjoy doing regularly in your free time

29. What are notes? (1 mark)
   A. Songs
   B. Long stories
   C. Short records of important points
   D. Pictures only

30. Which of these can begin a happy line? (1 mark)
   A. Oh no!
   B. Ouch!
   C. Yuck!
   D. Hurray!

31. What is a singing game with interjections? (1 mark)
   A. A silent game
   B. A song where short exclamations show joy or surprise
   C. A story
   D. A written test

32. What is good telephone manner? (1 mark)
   A. Speaking clearly and giving your name
   B. Interrupting
   C. Calling very late for no reason
   D. Speaking with food in your mouth

33. Which device is used mainly to take photographs? (1 mark)
   A. Camera
   B. Radio
   C. Torch
   D. Clock

34. What is a headline? (1 mark)
   A. The last word
   B. A price
   C. A short eye-catching title
   D. A picture

35. What does the lead of a news item give? (1 mark)
   A. The main facts
   B. A joke
   C. A poem
   D. The ending

36. What is a form? (1 mark)
   A. A picture
   B. A page with spaces for information
   C. A kind of song
   D. A story

37. Which field asks how old you are? (1 mark)
   A. Age
   B. Signature
   C. Class
   D. School

38. Which is a polite phrase for asking someone to explain again? (1 mark)
   A. Never mind
   B. You are silly
   C. Say it again now
   D. Pardon me, could you explain?

39. What is a talking object used for? (1 mark)
   A. To show who may speak
   B. To play with
   C. To hide
   D. To throw

40. What does turn taking mean? (1 mark)
   A. Speaking loudest
   B. Speaking all at once
   C. Refusing to speak
   D. Speaking one at a time and waiting for your chance

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Write a five-line role play dialogue on personal safety between a child and a stranger. Show the speaker names and use question marks correctly. (5 marks)

42. Give three uses of capital letters in English. (3 marks)

43. Explain what turn taking means. (2 marks)

44. Name four question words used to check comprehension. (2 marks)

45. Explain what a subject and a predicate are, then write one sentence and divide it. (5 marks)

46. Explain how to work out the meaning of an unknown word using context. (4 marks)

47. Explain two differences between an advert and a news item. (4 marks)

48. Give three good manners to show when collecting proverbs from an elder. (3 marks)

49. Name two prepositions used to show position. (2 marks)

50. Put in order: shillings the pays customer fifty (3 marks)

51. Give two adjectives to describe a mobile phone. (2 marks)

52. Write three sentences describing where things are in your classroom. Use a different preposition in each. (3 marks)

53. State three rules for a debate. (3 marks)

54. State three benefits of reading widely. (3 marks)

55. Write one correct line of a dialogue with a speaker name and an interjection. (2 marks)

56. Explain how the language train game is played. (4 marks)

57. Name three parts of a simple form. (3 marks)

58. Give two reasons why neat handwriting matters. (2 marks)

59. Give three questions to ask when reading an advert. (3 marks)

60. Give two reasons why we read fluently. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #9 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — So the songs are kept safe and are not forgotten
   A portfolio preserves the songs collected from the community.

2. D — How should we respond to instructions?
   The lesson asks how we should respond to instructions in songs and games.

3. C — Say one good thing and one thing to improve
   Kind and useful feedback helps people improve.

4. A — They let you practise a word and its meaning again and again
   Flashcards are a simple tool for revision.

5. D — g
   The letter g has a tail that goes below the line.

6. D — It rises
   Many questions end with a rising voice.

7. A — clearly and at a steady pace
   News should be clear and easy to follow.

8. D — Using a comma where a full stop is needed
   A comma cannot join two complete sentences on its own.

9. A — Sitting where you can see and hear the speaker
   You can follow better when you see and hear clearly.

10. D — Who
   Who asks about people.

11. C — Look right, then left, then right again
   The dialogue teaches how to look before crossing.

12. D — Very crowded
   The matatu could not move because there was too much traffic.

13. A — First, boil the water.
   Boiling water is the first step.

14. C — Read it aloud
   Reading aloud shows if the order makes sense.

15. D — like and as
   Similes use like or as.

16. C — The classroom was a beehive.
   A metaphor says one thing is another.

17. C — She is as bright as the sun.
   It uses as to compare.

18. D — A short play
   A skit is a short acted scene.

19. C — Listen politely and give kind feedback
   Respect is important.

20. D — A person who buys
   A customer buys goods or services.

21. A — Reading quickly to get the main idea
   Skimming gives the general idea.

22. D — One subject and one predicate
   Simple sentences have one main idea.

23. C — To discuss the price
   Bargaining is agreeing on price.

24. A — before something and facing it
   In front of shows the position ahead of something.

25. D — Goat
   Goats are kept by people.

26. B — says the poem together at the same pace
   Choral means together.

27. A — Look at the audience and speak clearly
   Eye contact and clarity help.

28. D — Something you enjoy doing regularly in your free time
   A hobby is a regular enjoyable activity.

29. C — Short records of important points
   Notes are brief points.

30. D — Hurray!
   Hurray shows happiness.

31. B — A song where short exclamations show joy or surprise
   Interjections can be part of songs.

32. A — Speaking clearly and giving your name
   Clarity and courtesy help.

33. A — Camera
   A camera takes photos.

34. C — A short eye-catching title
   A headline is the title of an advert or news item.

35. A — The main facts
   The lead gives the key facts.

36. B — A page with spaces for information
   Forms collect information.

37. A — Age
   Age records how old you are.

38. D — Pardon me, could you explain?
   Pardon me and could you are polite.

39. A — To show who may speak
   Only the holder speaks.

40. D — Speaking one at a time and waiting for your chance
   Turn taking is orderly speaking.

SECTION B
----
41. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any five correct lines, for example Child: Good afternoon. Stranger: Do you want a ride? Child: No, thank you. I will wait for my mother. Stranger: Are you sure? Child: Yes, I am telling my teacher.
   Working / marking points: One mark for speaker names, one for a safe message, one for correct questions and two for five clear lines.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: The first word of a sentence, names of people and places, the word I, days and months (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each use.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: It means speaking one person at a time and waiting for others to finish before speaking.
   Working / marking points: One mark for one at a time and one for waiting.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Who, what, where, when, why, how (any four).
   Working / marking points: One mark for two correct question words and two marks for four.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: The subject is who or what the sentence is about and the predicate says what the subject does. Example: The girl (subject) counts the coins (predicate).
   Working / marking points: Two marks for the two meanings, one for a sentence, and two marks for the correct division.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Read the sentence with the word, look at nearby words for clues, guess a meaning, check that it makes sense in the sentence and confirm in a dictionary.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: An advert aims to persuade people to buy, while news informs about events. An advert gives a price and where to buy, while news gives who, what, where and when.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for each difference.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Greet politely, listen without interrupting, ask permission to write, say thank you.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: on, in, under, behind, beside, between, in front of, outside (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: The customer pays fifty shillings.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the words in order, one for the capital and one for the full stop.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: small, black, thin, new, flat (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sensible adjective.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Any three correct sentences, for example The board is in front of the class. My bag is under my desk. The teacher stands beside the door.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct sentence.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen without interrupting, speak politely, give reasons, accept the result graciously, take turns.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: It builds vocabulary, improves spelling, gives new ideas, makes you a better writer and speaker, gives enjoyment.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each benefit.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: Neema: Wow! The sun is shining.
   Working / marking points: One mark for name with colon and one for an interjection.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: A pupil starts with a sentence. Each next pupil continues the story with a sentence beginning with when until the story ends.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Title, instructions, fields, signature, date.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: It helps the reader to understand the message, and it shows respect and builds confidence.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sensible reason.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: What is being sold, who is it for, what is the price, where can I get it, is it as good as it says.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: It helps listeners understand and enjoy, and it helps the reader to understand the text.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each reason.
